EXPLAINER: Protecting the Skies: How Poland’s Proposed No-Fly Zone Could Work — Poland plans to establish a no-fly zone along its eastern borders with Ukraine and Belarus after Russian missiles and drones entered its airspace. The restrictions could help its military respond to incursions, while authorities say passenger flights should remain unaffected.

Trump Appears to Confuse Israel With Iran, Says ‘Their Military Is Decimated’ — Trump appeared to confuse Israel with Iran while answering a question about Israeli PM Netanyahu and the country’s next leadership. He described a military as “decimated” before turning to Iran’s nuclear facilities.

Ukraine Strikes Rocket Fuel Plant in Russia’s Tula Region as Drones Hit St. Petersburg — Ukrainian drones targeted energy and industrial facilities in Russia’s Tula region and struck areas of St. Petersburg, where a residential building was reportedly damaged. Moscow claimed its air defenses intercepted 318 drones overnight.

British-Ukrainian Defense Tech Startup Pai Defence Raises $5M for Drone Detection System — British-Ukrainian defense startup Pai Defence has secured $5 million in pre-seed funding led by Nordic venture fund Gardar, alongside nine Ukraine-focused venture capitalists. The company will use the funds to expand frontline sensor coverage and advance its machine learning systems that track and predict enemy drone behavior in real time.

UK to Invest £9.5 Million in Ukraine Wind Farm to Be Built by Elementum Energy — The UK is to invest £9.5 million ($12.4 million) in a 200 MW wind farm in Ukraine capable of powering 300,000 households. Elementum Energy, a renewable power producer belonging to Richard Deitz’s VR Global Partners, is expected to build and operate the facility. The investment adds to British support for an energy system heavily damaged by Russian attacks.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 26, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 26, 2026.

‘It’s Like Being Friends With Adolf Hitler’: Zelensky Questions Trump’s Friendship With Putin — President Volodymyr Zelensky drew a parallel with Adolf Hitler during World War II when questioning US President Donald Trump’s friendship with Russian President Vladimir Putin. In a wide-ranging BBC interview, Zelensky argued that neutrality toward an aggressor enables further bloodshed. He criticized Washington for prioritizing the Middle East while Ukraine faces critical air defense shortages, addr

Trump Says Putin Is Welcome at G20 Despite Bipartisan Calls to Rescind Invitation — US President Donald Trump said Thursday that Russian President Vladimir Putin could attend next month’s G20 summit in Florida if he wished. Trump acknowledged opposition to Putin’s participation but said he personally would welcome him. Bipartisan groups of US senators and congressmen have urged the administration to withdraw the invitation, citing Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and assistance to Iran.

UK Slams Russia’s ‘Baseless’ Nazi Rhetoric to Justify War Against Ukraine — Britain has condemned Russia’s use of baseless accusations of Nazism to justify its aggression against Ukraine. British Ambassador to the OSCE Neil Holland called the rhetoric deeply disrespectful to millions who suffered under Nazi rule. He outlined how Moscow had violated successive international security agreements it freely negotiated and signed. Holland also rejected Russia’s demands for a new European security orde

Russia Is Preparing Another Massive Strike on Ukraine, Zelensky Warns — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russia was preparing another massive strike on Ukraine in the coming days, targeting energy infrastructure, logistics and essential services. He urged Ukrainians to heed air raid alerts and vowed retaliation against Russian attacks. Kyiv is seeking additional air defense support from international partners as the delivery of 48 US Patriot interceptor missiles remains stalled.

France Defends Ukraine’s Strikes on Russian Vessels off Libya — France has defended Ukraine’s drone strikes on two Russian vessels off the Libyan coast. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Ukraine was exercising its “absolute right to self-defense” against Russian aggression. He questioned how other countries would respond if subjected to relentless bombardment by an invading force. His remarks come as Ukraine expands its military operations against Russian assets far beyond the Black

Trump Revises NATO Statement, Adds Ukraine to Escalation Warning — US President Donald Trump has altered the wording of a joint statement issued following his meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. While the original text called on Russia to avoid expanding the war, Trump’s version extended the warning to Ukraine. A NATO official confirmed that both sides had agreed to the original wording.

Canadian Auto Factories Could Soon Build Weapons for Ukraine — Canadian auto parts manufacturers and Ukraine’s defense industry have signed a memorandum on joint military production. The agreement could see Canadian factories manufacture drones, interceptors, unmanned ground vehicles and electronic warfare systems. The initiative would combine Ukrainian battlefield expertise with Canada’s industrial capacity.

Ukraine Rushes Generators to Dnipro as Russia Targets Grid Repairs — Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy will deliver seven high-capacity diesel generators to the Dnipropetrovsk region on Friday, Nov. 27, First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said, after repeated Russian strikes on substations left Dnipro and nearby communities facing prolonged outages. Around the same time on Thursday, Nov. 26, President Volodymyr Zelensky named Dnipro and Pavlohrad among the hardest-hit areas

Suspect Detained Over Kharkiv Army Major’s Killing, SBU Alleges Russian Contract — Working together, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and the National Police have detained a 23-year-old man from the Vinnytsia region on suspicion of killing a 28-year-old army major in Kharkiv on Nov. 22. According to the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), Russian intelligence recruited the suspect via Telegram, offered him $15,000 for the killing and guided him through a live video call during the attack, wh

Race for Super-Fast Interceptor Drones Gathers Speed — Two manufacturers building interceptor drones intended to take on Russia’s Geran jet-powered UAVs have broken speed records in the space of four days this week. The Ukraine based Quantum WIY Industries “SPYS interceptor” broke the national speed record on Nov. 23, while Quantum’s “Apex Recordhunter” set a world’s best in Germany three days later as they attempt to develop the necessary counter-measures.

Hungary: Last in EU to Join Coalition for Ukraine’s Deported Children — Hungary has joined the International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children, Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced on Thursday, Nov. 26, making all 27 EU member states part of the initiative. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha welcomed the move – which came after Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s first visit to Ukraine – as a signal of European unity.

Trump Says He Urged Putin to Halt Aggression in Europe — US President Donald Trump said on Thursday, Nov. 26 that he had pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe during their first trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. In the same remarks, he called a quick Russia-Ukraine deal “a strong possibility.”

Lithuania Seeks EU Terrorist Label for Russia’s GRU Spy Agency — Lithuania is pushing for the EU to designate Russia’s Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) as a terrorist organization, citing its alleged involvement in cyberattacks, sabotage and other covert activities. The agency has been accused of cyberattacks targeting Ukrainian government agencies and explosions at a Czech arms factory in 2014.

Nearly Half of Captured Foreign Recruits Knew They’d Fight Ukraine, Survey Says — Nearly half of captured foreign recruits surveyed by Ukraine’s “I Want to Live” project said they knew before signing a Russian contract that they would fight. Only 1.7% said they were coerced or deceived into signing. Russian citizenship was the most cited motive. The project did not disclose the sample size or survey dates, and answers given in captivity may be shaped by respondents’ circumstances.

Czech President Urges NATO to Shoot Down Russian Weapons in Allied Airspace — Czech President Petr Pavel said NATO should be ready to shoot down Russian drones and missiles repeatedly violating allied airspace. Speaking to senators on Thursday, he urged a response Moscow would understand and said Russia would act similarly. His comments follow recent incursions into Poland. Warsaw is seeking stronger defenses, while a separate proposal to intercept Russian weapons over Ukraine remains unsupporte

Italy Summons Ukrainian Military Envoy Over Libya Strikes — Italy summoned Ukraine’s military attaché on Wednesday over Ukrainian strikes on Russian ships near Benghazi, Libya, according to Italian media. Ukraine’s ambassador accompanied him to the meeting. Rome is also considering stronger protection for about 200 Italian troops in Libya. Kyiv defends the strikes as self-defense under the UN Charter, while Rome warns against spreading Russia’s war against Ukraine to the Mediterranean.

Blackout Hits Nearly All of Crimea, Halts Trams, Heating — Widespread power cuts hit Russian-occupied Crimea on Nov. 26, disrupting heating and public transport. Russian-controlled utilities blamed a failure at energy facilities outside the peninsula without identifying the affected infrastructure. Parts of Kerch lost heating, while electric transport was disrupted in other cities. The outage followed the introduction of electricity restrictions that occupation authorities said could last up to

Ukraine Receives $450M in World Bank Funding for Business Support, Reconstruction — Ukraine has received $450 million in results-based World Bank financing guaranteed by Japan, with $225 million for small and medium-sized business development and $225 million to strengthen public investment management and climate-focused reconstruction. The funding builds on broader World Bank programs launched in 2024.

Oil Refinery in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory Struck Again Amid Repairs in Overnight Ukrainian Blitz — Ukraine struck the Slavyansk oil refinery in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory early morning on Nov. 26, causing significant damage to processing equipment, pipelines and oil storage facilities while the plant was still undergoing repairs following a previous Ukrainian attack. The strike was part of a wider overnight operation targeting Russian military and energy infrastructure, including an airfiel

Ukraine Prepares ‘Santa’ Mission to Bring Aid to Civilians Trapped on Occupied Kinburn Spit — Ukraine’s military is preparing a humanitarian mission dubbed “Santa” to deliver food and medicine to civilians on the occupied Kinburn Spit. The initiative comes as Kyiv also identifies 15 settlements in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions for potential evacuation.

Ukraine Brings Home 250 More War Dead in New Exchange — Ukraine has received the bodies of 250 people whom Russia claims were Ukrainian servicemen, the Coordination Headquarters for Treatment of Prisoners of War said on Thursday, Nov. 26. Ukrainian investigators and forensic specialists will work to identify the remains following the latest repatriation operation, which involved several government agencies and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

Ukrainian Military Radio Maker Himera Raises $5M — Ukrainian military radio maker Himera has raised $5 million in a round led by Norwegian defense fund Gardar. Existing investors Varangians, Bulava and Green Flag VC took part, along with new backers Superangel and Next Front Ventures. The company says it will use the money to develop new products, scale its systems for Ukraine’s Defense Forces and expand abroad. Founded in 2022, Himera makes radios and repeaters designed to work under Russian ja

Russia Nears Final Preparations for New Strike on Ukraine’s Critical Infrastructure — Zelensky says Russia is finalizing preparations for another massive strike on Ukraine, with energy, logistics, and essential infrastructure among the expected targets. He also called for more air defense interceptors and announced plans for new sanctions on Russia’s ballistic weapons industry.

Russian Su-34 Base Hit in Volgograd Oblast as Ukraine Steps Up Deep Strikes on Airfields — Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck Russia’s Marinovka military airfield in the Volgograd region with Neptune missiles overnight on Nov. 26, targeting a base used by Su-34 fighter-bombers. The attack came a day after Kyiv confirmed hitting five aircraft at another Russian airfield, Savasleyka, as Ukraine steps up strikes against Russian military aviation.

Stubb Doubts Year-End Peace, Urges Winter Aid for Ukraine — Finnish President Alexander Stubb expressed doubt that Russia’s war against Ukraine would end before the end of 2026. In a Nov. 18 Bloomberg interview, he urged preparations for a difficult winter, prioritizing air defenses, energy infrastructure and financing. He also called for sustained diplomatic efforts. His assessment comes as Kyiv seeks additional military support and warns against pressure to accept an unfavorable peace agreemen

UK Contacts 100,000 Reservists as Russia Threat Raises War Fears — Britain has contacted around 100,000 former military personnel in its first major Strategic Reserve outreach since the Cold War. The initiative aims to strengthen military readiness amid growing concerns over Russian threats to NATO, although the government insists there are no plans for immediate mobilization.

Russia Arrests Aerospace Forces General on Bribery Charges as Military Purge Continues — Russia has arrested Aerospace Forces Deputy Commander Yuri Grekhov on large-scale bribery charges as Ukrainian drone and missile strikes expose weaknesses in the country’s air defenses. The arrest comes amid a wider purge of senior Russian military officials following Sergei Shoigu’s departure as defense minister in 2024.

Finland, Norway Called Putin to Ease Baltic Sea Tensions — Finland and Norway’s leaders called Putin in October to avert a Baltic Sea clash and reassure him they had no plans for a blockade, the Wall Street Journal reported. The leaders sought to reassure Moscow that they had no plans to block a shipping route that carries more than 60% of Russia’s oil.

Z-Blogger Questions Combat Value of Russia’s Su-57 Stealth Fighter — Russia’s state aircraft maker, United Aircraft Corporation, called the Su-57 “Felon” the country’s “main” combat aircraft as it delivered the latest batch to Moscow’s aerospace forces a week ago. However, the pro-Kremlin milblogger, “Fighterbomber,” said they played a minor role in the war in Ukraine, adding if they vanished tomorrow, “no one would notice.”

North Korea Halts Military Aid to Russia, Ukraine’s Intel Says — North Korea has temporarily suspended its military assistance to Russia following a diplomatic dispute over Moscow’s intention to ease tensions between Pyongyang and Seoul, Ukraine’s military intelligence said. The reported restrictions include KN-23 ballistic missiles, artillery ammunition and the use of North Korean airspace by Russian military transport aircraft. Pyongyang is also delaying a Russian request to expand its troop d

Ukraine Contacts Family After Warsaw Self-Immolation — Ukraine’s embassy in Poland has contacted the mother of a 22-year-old man hospitalized after setting himself alight near Warsaw’s Presidential Palace on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Diplomats are assisting the family and communicating with Polish police. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said he was likely Ukrainian, although identification procedures remained underway. The man is in intensive care, and investigators have not confirmed a motive.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Oil Pipeline Hub, Refinery and Power Plant in Overnight Blitz Across Russia — Ukrainian drones struck critical energy and industrial infrastructure in at least three Russian regions overnight on Thursday, setting fires at an oil pipeline station in Bashkortostan and an oil refinery in Samara, while also targeting a major power plant in Stavropol Territory.

Spanish Election: What’s at Stake? — Spain’s snap election could reshape its political landscape, with the conservative Popular Party seeking to replace Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s government, potentially with Vox’s support. The campaign has focused on housing, immigration, public services and corruption, while European policy has taken a back seat.

Russian Strike Kills 3 in Kharkiv as Moscow Pounds Ukraine with Ballistic Missiles, 100+ Drones — Russian drone strikes killed 3 people and injured several others in Kharkiv, while attacks across Dnipropetrovsk region injured one man and damaged civilian and energy infrastructure. Russia also launched 113 drones and several types of missiles at Ukraine overnight.

‘We Are At War’: Kasparov Urges Europe to Build Defense Coalition Independent of US — Russian opposition figure Kasparov has urged Europe to form a new defense coalition with Ukraine, Poland and other European countries, arguing that the continent cannot rely on US leadership under President Donald Trump to counter Russia.

Ukraine Strikes Major Russian Power Plant Supplying Electricity to North Caucasus — Ukrainian drones struck the Nevinnomyssk power plant in Russia’s Stavropol Krai, which supplies electricity to much of the North Caucasus. The attack comes amid a broader campaign against Russian energy infrastructure, with refinery output falling and fuel restrictions introduced in at least 16 regions.

‘I’m Fine’: The Hidden Psychological Wounds of Ukraine’s War-Wounded — A new study of wounded Ukrainian service members reveals a troubling gap between the trauma they carry and the support they receive, as many turn to fellow soldiers rather than psychologists and face a compensation system that can reward administrative status over the severity of their injuries.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 25, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 25, 2026.

Trump, Rutte Warn Russia Against Escalation, Call for Swift Peace in Ukraine — US President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte warned Russia against actions that could expand its war against Ukraine following talks at Mar-a-Lago. The two leaders stressed the importance of securing a peaceful resolution as rapidly as possible. They also reaffirmed the need to increase defense spending and investment in defense production across NATO. The meeting followed Trump’s talks with Vladimi

Kushner Admits Putin Is Not Interested in Ceasefire, Urges Zelensky to Respect Trump — Jared Kushner acknowledged that Vladimir Putin remains uninterested in a ceasefire while suggesting that Volodymyr Zelensky should engage with Donald Trump respectfully to secure US security guarantees. Trump’s envoy characterized Russia’s invasion of Ukraine as a “proxy war” and praised Putin as a “grandmaster of politics.” Kushner said territorial negotiations remained deadlocked, arguing that a settlement w

Halt ‘Shameful’ $10B Lukoil Deal, Top House Democrat Demands of Trump — Congressman Gregory Meeks demanded that the Trump administration immediately halt US government involvement in a proposed $10 billion acquisition of Lukoil’s international assets. The top House Foreign Affairs Democrat warned that the transaction circumvents congressional restrictions on investments in Russia, empowers Moscow and undercuts Ukraine. Congressional concerns over the acquisition have crossed party lines, with Se

Pentagon Offers No Answers on Delayed Patriot Deliveries to Ukraine — The Pentagon says it is working with European partners and Ukraine to expand Patriot production but neither confirmed nor denied reports of delayed interceptor deliveries. President Volodymyr Zelensky revealed that 48 already-funded Patriot missiles still await US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s approval.

Russia Hits Kyiv Shopping Mall With Ballistic Missiles, Injures 7 — Russia launched another ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late Wednesday, Nov. 25, injuring seven people. A shopping mall and other non-residential buildings were hit in the capital’s Desnianskyi district. Two victims were previously reported to be in serious condition. The attack comes amid continued delays in US deliveries of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine.

Ukraine’s Blysk Laser Destroys Russian Jet-Powered Shahed for First Time — Ukraine has shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone for the first time with a combat laser, presidential adviser Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov said on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The Blysk system, developed by Carmine Sky under the state Private Air Defense program, is protecting critical infrastructure, though tests are ongoing and serial production remains premature.

US Billionaire Boehly Signs Deal for Lukoil’s Foreign Assets — US billionaire Todd Boehly said on Wednesday, Nov. 25 that he had signed a deal for a consortium including the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to acquire sanctioned Russian oil giant Lukoil’s international assets by swapping $10 billion in Lukoil securities, according to Reuters. The agreement, which needs US Treasury approval, comes amid warming US-Russia economic ties.

Ukraine Delays Yellow-Alert Shelter Rules for Businesses — Ukraine’s government has extended a transitional period allowing businesses without shelters to keep operating during yellow-level air alerts until June 4, 2027, subject to employee consent and safety measures. After that, premises with 100 or more people will be required to provide a fully equipped shelter.

NATO Turns to AI to Link Allied Weapon Systems — Artificial intelligence (AI) could improve communication between NATO allies’ weapon systems, Supreme Allied Commander Transformation Admiral Pierre Vandier said in Brussels on Wednesday, Nov. 25. According to him, AI is already helping Ukrainian Defense Forces identify targets on the battlefield, while warning that reliance on commercial cloud providers raises serious concerns over protecting classified data.

EU Curbs Exports to 15 Russian Defense Companies — The Council of the EU has added 15 Russian entities linked to Moscow’s military-industrial complex to its list of companies facing tighter export controls on dual-use goods and advanced technologies, while removing one. The measure, added on Wednesday, Nov. 25, follows the EU’s largest sanctions listings in October, as Brussels seeks a direct role in peace negotiations with Russia.

Trump to Meet NATO Chief in Florida — US President Donald Trump is set to meet NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Florida on Wednesday, Nov. 25, days after calling Russian President Vladimir Putin his “friend” during a visit to China. Rutte said Trump was “testing Putin” and stressed that any deal must include security guarantees for Ukraine, while President Volodymyr Zelensky responded that, for Ukrainians, Putin “is a killer.”

Russian Assets Frozen in Switzerland Rise to $10.2B — Russian assets frozen in Switzerland have climbed to 8.5 billion Swiss francs (about $10.2 billion), marking a 15% rise since April 2025, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, Nov. 25, citing Swiss sanctions chief Daniel Aeby. The increase reflects new seizures and higher gold prices, while frozen Russian central bank assets fell in value due to currency changes.

Ukraine Passes Long-Awaited Law to Regulate Crypto Market — Ukraine's parliament on Nov. 25 passed a law regulating the country's crypto market, which until now has had no specific rules. The securities commission will license and supervise most service providers, while the National Bank will oversee e-money token issuers and crypto-to-cash exchanges. Preliminary authorizations can begin May 1, 2027, and the main provisions take effect July 1, 2027.

Budanov: First Stage of Major POW Swap Could Take Place Soon — Budanov said the first stage of a planned exchange involving 1,000 people could take place in late November or early December. The broader effort also aims to return civilians from occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions.

Kerch Bridge All Week but NATO Was Stupid Again — Ukraine brought down part of the Kerch Bridge in three nights of drone and missile strikes, leaving Crimea's Russian garrison facing a logistics crisis heading into winter. Meanwhile, NATO flew its biggest reconnaissance surge over the Black Sea of the war – yet failed to stop Russian drones sinking merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria or missiles entering Poland.

Kremlin Says ‘Disregard’ Reports of 700,000 Russian Dead — Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov urged people to disregard independent estimates that more than 700,000 Russian troops have died in the war against Ukraine. He said only Russia’s Defense Ministry could release casualty figures. His comments followed a Meduza and Mediazona investigation identifying approximately 490,000 registered military deaths through September 2026, with higher estimates accounting for delayed registrations and prob

Britain Shelters RAF Aircraft Overnight Amid Fears of Russian Drone Attacks — The British Royal Air Force (RAF) is moving aircraft into hangars and hardened shelters overnight and considering anti-drone netting to protect warplanes. The measures come amid increasing security concerns, suspected hostile drone activity at UK military bases and warnings of potential Russian sabotage against British defense facilities supporting Ukraine.

The Economics of the Sky: Why Ukraine Cannot Afford a Missile-For-Missile War — Russia now builds more ballistic missiles than the US and Europe together produce interceptors to stop them. Ukraine cannot win the air war by interception alone, with expensive missiles or cheap drones. Its 2027 budget, which parliament votes on this week, has not caught up with that arithmetic yet, and there are only days left to change it.

Von der Leyen: Europe Will Join Next Round of Talks With Russia — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said a European team will take part in the next round of negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. She also announced new sanctions proposals and extra funding for Kyiv, while the Kremlin says it has not agreed to a European presence at the talks.

Poland Urges NATO to Down Russian Missiles Over Ukraine — Poland has asked NATO allies to consider intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine if they are heading toward alliance territory, Bloomberg reported. Warsaw raised the proposal during talks in Brussels after three Russian missiles crashed in Poland on Friday. Some allies supported discussing the idea, but no decision was reached. Polish ministers argue that earlier interceptions could protect their country, while allies remain concerned

Kyiv Bids Farewell to Vyacheslav Briukhovetsky, Who Revived the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy — Hundreds of people, including academics, colleagues and former students, gathered at the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy to bid farewell to Vyacheslav Briukhovetsky, the intellectual and educator who revived the historic institution in 1992. Remembered for his commitment to academic freedom, openness and dialogue with students, Briukhovetsky also played a prominent role in Ukraine’s intellectual and political life during t

Ukraine Destroys Russia’s Aerospace Recon System in New Deep Strike — Ukraine’s Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR) says it has destroyed Russia’s MRIK-VKO aerospace reconnaissance complex in the Smolensk region. The facility supported Russian air and missile defense operations and was reportedly capable of detecting low-observable aircraft and cruise missiles within a 2,500-kilometer radius (1,553 miles).

Russian Attack on Odesa Injures 3, Damages Homes and Energy Infrastructure — A massive Russian drone attack on Odesa and its suburbs injured 3 people and damaged a residential complex, a logistics facility, and a household paper products plant. Parts of two Odesa districts lost power, while energy workers began restoring supply.

Ukraine’s Parliament Backs Joining Committee for Russian Aggression Tribunal — Ukraine’s parliament has approved legislation to join the management committee of the special tribunal established to prosecute Russia’s crime of aggression against Ukraine, with 293 lawmakers voting in favor. Membership would give Kyiv a role in funding and administrative decisions. Kyiv aims to have the Hague-based tribunal operational in 2027. The court is intended to prosecute senior leaders for the decision to wa

From Orbán to Magyar: How Hungary Recast Its Ukraine Policy — On his first visit to Ukraine as prime minister, Péter Magyar discussed minority rights, historical grievances, energy cooperation, and EU accession with President Zelensky. Budapest’s national interests have not fundamentally changed since Viktor Orbán’s departure, but the way Hungary pursues them has.

Russian Attacks Kill Civilians, Damage Kyiv Court, Hit Energy Sites — Russia launched 112 drones overnight into Wednesday, Ukraine’s Air Force said. A Kyiv courthouse and residential buildings were damaged, while a morning strike wounded six people in southern Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, including two children. Odesa authorities reported two deaths in evening attacks and power cuts affecting about 9,000 customers. Energy strikes also forced the occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant onto backup generat

One of Ukraine’s Best-Equipped Brigades Gets New KF41 Lynx IFV From Germany — Ukraine’s 21st Brigade has received five German KF41 Lynx IFVs for testing and combat, praising their mobility, sensors and 30mm cannon. The vehicles may eventually be built in Ukraine, but Rheinmetall’s factory plan remains unfunded.

Putin Calls for More Oil Refining in Siberia, Russia’s Far East — Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday told a meeting of his fuel and energy commission that Russia must develop oil refining in Siberia and the Far East. Ukrainian drones have attacked Russian refineries more than 110 times this year. Strikes in November alone have halted all or part of production at 16 refineries. Putin said retaliation was inevitable but did not specify what it would involve.

Russian Attack Cuts External Power Supply to Europe’s Largest Nuclear Power Plant — The Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in southern Ukraine lost its external electricity supply on Wednesday, Nov. 25, after a Russian attack damaged a nearby power line. Emergency diesel generators are supplying the facility’s essential needs, while the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) investigates the incident.

Germany Uses Attack Drones to Strike Russian-Style Tanks in First Live-Fire Exercise — Germany conducted its first live-fire drone warfare exercise in Lithuania, using kamikaze drones to strike Leopard 2 tanks simulating Russian armor. The demonstration showed progress in drone warfare but also exposed technical and training gaps.

Ukraine Says 3 MiG-31s, 2 Su-34s Hit at Russian Airfield, 2 Refineries Damaged — Ukraine’s General Staff confirmed that three MiG-31 fighter jets and two Su-34 fighter-bombers were hit at Russia’s Savasleyka military airfield in the Nizhny Novgorod region. The defense ministry also detailed damage to processing units and storage tanks at the Kuibyshev and Syzran oil refineries in the Samara region, both owned by Rosneft.

Running Scared? Russian Naval Convoy ‘Marks Time’ Near Tunisia — A five-vessel Russian naval convoy has been moving slowly off Tunisia’s coast for nearly a week, according to open-source tracking. Its original corvette escort was replaced by the more heavily armed frigate Admiral Golovko. Both changes came before the naval drone attack in Benghazi that Ukraine says sank the corvette Merkury. Observers have suggested Moscow is increasingly worried about threats to its shipping.

Paris Ready to Send Envoy to Moscow – Only if Europe Gets a Full Seat at Ukraine Talks — France says it will consider Putin’s invitation for talks in Moscow only if Russia guarantees Europe a full seat at the negotiating table. Officials from France, Germany, and the UK have discussed possible talks with the Kremlin.

Estonia’s Foreign Minister Arrives in Kyiv for Visit — Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna arrived in Ukraine on Wednesday, Nov. 25, for a visit. He shared footage from Kyiv on X. The visit comes as Estonia continues to support Ukraine amid Russia’s full-scale invasion, with Moscow threatening an “open war” with a Baltic state following Tallinn’s border closures.

Trump Officials Weigh Killing Iran’s Leaders — Trump administration officials are debating whether to target senior Iranian leaders to pressure Tehran into ending the war, NBC News reported on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Supporters argue that killing hardliners could create an opening for a settlement. Opponents warn that the operation could undermine negotiations and increase threats to American officials. Trump has not made a final decision as the conflict continues into its ninth month.

US Issues New Ukraine Travel Warning Over Russian Attacks — The US State Department renewed its warning against travel to Ukraine a day after an American was hospitalized in Kyiv, citing Russian missile and drone attacks and potential restrictions on Ukrainian dual citizens. Americans in the country are urged to monitor air alerts, locate shelters and enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP).

Kremlin Accuses Estonia of Aiding Ukrainian Drone Strikes, Warns of 'Open War' — Russia warned Estonia that its actions were bringing the countries to the brink of “open war” after Tallinn announced a six-month border closure. Moscow also accused Estonia of helping Ukraine launch drone attacks, a claim Estonia rejected.

Russia Turns to China for Inflatable Fighter Jets and Tanks to Fool Ukrainian Drones — Russia has imported at least $120 million in goods under a Chinese customs code used by inflatable military decoy manufacturers since February 2022, The Telegraph reported. The products help Moscow mislead Ukrainian drones and protect real military equipment.

Ukrainian Drones Hit 2 Major Oil Refineries in Samara as Putin Urges Oil Industry Shift East — Ukraine’s overnight drone attack hit two major Russian oil refineries in Samara Region, adding to a campaign that has disrupted 16 facilities since early November. As Russian refining capacity comes under growing pressure, Putin is urging oil companies to expand production in Siberia and the Far East.

Ukraine Hits Targets in the Baltic and off Libya — Ukraine’s expanding naval drone capabilities are putting increasing pressure on Russia, demonstrating its ability to strike military and supply vessels far beyond the front lines. European commentators highlight Ukraine’s right to self-defence while warning of escalation risks, threats to Baltic security, and potential environmental damage. The attacks also expose weaknesses in Russia’s military logistics and overseas operations.

Ukrainian Skaters Win Cheers at Skate America as War Shuts Rinks at Home — Ukrainian figure skaters competing at Skate America in Everett, Washington, were greeted by fans waving Ukrainian flags. Ice dancers Iryna Pidgaina and Artem Koval, who left Ukraine after the 2022 invasion, said their results show support for their country. Skaters still training at home face air raid alerts and rinks destroyed by Russian strikes.

Vladyslav Yerko, Renowned Ukrainian Illustrator, to Be Celebrated in Kyiv Exhibition — The exhibition “Vladyslav Yerko: The Memory of an Image” is running at Ukrainskiy Dim (Ukrainian House) in Kyiv from Nov. 26-Dec. 6. It will feature the celebrated Ukrainian illustrator’s iconic works for Ukrainian and international literary classics, alongside original sketches. The project explores how book illustrations shape personal and collective memory, preserve childhood experiences, and create lasting
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 24, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 24, 2026.

Pentagon Has Yet to Sign Off on 48 Patriot Missiles for Ukraine, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said an agreement to deliver 48 Patriot interceptors remains unsigned on US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s desk, despite allied funding. Ukraine also has yet to receive licenses to manufacture Patriot missiles despite assurances from President Donald Trump. Zelensky criticized delays in weapons deliveries amid ongoing peace negotiations and confirmed that restrictions on Starshield rem

Russia Bombards Bila Tserkva, Killing 1, Damaging Facilities — A Russian overnight attack killed one person in Bila Tserkva, Kyiv region, on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The strikes damaged critical infrastructure and several civilian businesses, including Epicentr and Nova Poshta facilities. The attack follows Russian strikes on energy infrastructure in two districts of the Kyiv region on Tuesday.

Trump Administration Undermines Kushner’s Ukraine Security Proposal, Ex-US Envoy Warns — Former US Ambassador Daniel Fried warned that the Trump administration’s policies contradict Jared Kushner’s proposed Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine. Fried argued that a legally binding US defense commitment could provide a foundation for lasting peace.
